title: How the trombone has been held back
summary: Writers give trombones little; Durham says it has 14 positions, not seven, and wants to bring out more of what it can do.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: -- the development of the trombone, since you first started out -- I mean, what's happened to it? Apart from the --
Well, they always held the trombone back by trying to make an ________ instrument out of it, like a ________, which is supposed to tail along slow.

But trombone players are fast. I guess about any player on trombone, you can (inaudible) on an alto. That's the way to do it. And it's been done. But the trombones (inaudible) back, because when they write, they don't ever write nothing for the trombone player. They got to stretch out. They played it back cheap. So I've always had in mind, I'd probably do something with the trombone family, because there's a lot in trombones that's never been brought out. Nobody ever bothered with it because it's a hard instrument and the only little thing I brought out, Don Redman started into that, little stuff, and I started into it a little bit with that slip-on, jive trick stuff and that's about as
far as I went, but I knew that a lot more can be done with those horns.
Well, Duke did it, too, with -- when he got Lawrence, didn't he?
He started doing like slippery horn and things like that, with the three trombones.

Yeah, but he didn't go too far with it, either. He didn't ever try to go too far (inaudible) just had time to really make a study of it. But in order to do it for the trombones, you should be a trombone player. (Inaudible) advanced on it. See, like I know there's 14 positions on it. There's still a seventh. That's how you can get so many things that the trombone players don't know.
Well, when you say there were 14 instead of seven, there was sort of officially seven.

It's officially seven, three inches apart. I play a inch and a half apart with solo work and everything else that had notes. You can execute and you can do things, but you got to have somebody with pretty good range.

One or two guys with good range, you can do anything you can do with anything else. There's a lot in them and you got a lot of fix and Duke Ellington, I give him credit because he started out with so many different effects
